title: Kinetic Energy
body:
**Kinetic energy** is the energy an object has because it is moving.

$$
KE = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2
$$

```
10 kg at 5 m/s:    ½ × 10 × 25 = 125 J
the same mass at 10 m/s:  ½ × 10 × 100 = 500 J
```

It is a scalar, so it has no direction and never goes negative, and it depends on the square of
the speed. Doubling the speed quadruples the energy, which is why stopping distance grows
faster than speed does and why a small increase in highway speed is a large increase in
collision energy.

The [[Work-Energy Theorem]] is what connects it to force, and [[Collisions]] is where its
conservation stops holding while momentum's continues.
